taxa.name: Hominins — maker or lineage unassigned
taxa.meaning: Evidence of hominin activity or remains whose biological species is not securely identified.
taxa.note: An indexing category, not a biological species or an ancestral branch. A stone-tool tradition alone does not identify its makers, ethnicity or language.

evidence.title: Aïn Boucherit: lower Oldowan horizon, Algeria
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Stone tools and modified animal bones document hominin activity at AB-Lw.
evidence.limits: The age is a stratigraphic estimate. No diagnostic hominin fossil identifies the toolmakers. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Aïn Boucherit: upper Oldowan horizon, Algeria
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: AB-Up is a separate, younger tool-and-fauna horizon in the Oued Boucherit sequence.
evidence.limits: Two excavated horizons do not demonstrate continuous residence between them. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Aïn Hanech: Oldowan occupation, Algeria
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Oldowan artefacts occur in the younger part of the regional sedimentary sequence.
evidence.limits: Magnetostratigraphic and faunal correlation date the context rather than an individual occupation event. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: El Kherba: Oldowan tools and carcass processing, Algeria
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A distinct locality near Aïn Hanech preserves tools and evidence of animal processing.
evidence.limits: The generalized point shares the same mapped research area; it is not the Aïn Hanech assemblage counted twice. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Tighennif: early hominin fossils, Algeria
evidence.dateBasis: Later faunal reassessment suggests at least ~1 Ma; this minimum is a display anchor. Neither a closed age range nor exact calendar chronology is established.
evidence.summary: Mandibles and other hominin remains occur with an Acheulean assemblage; their precise taxonomic placement remains debated.
evidence.limits: The older ~700 ka estimate and later ≥1 Ma interpretation differ. The point marks the proposed minimum-age threshold, not a securely dated instant or a proven ancestor. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Thomas Quarry I: Unit L Acheulean, Morocco
evidence.dateLabel: At least ~1.3 Ma; Unit L chronostratigraphy
evidence.dateBasis: Magnetostratigraphy and geochemical correlation constrain Unit L to at least ~1.3 Ma. Threshold-only visual placement, not an exact occupation date.
evidence.summary: Acheulean toolmaking is documented in an older, stratified part of the Casablanca quarry.
evidence.limits: This occupation context is distinct from the younger cave fossils. A minimum-age estimate does not identify a first arrival. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Thomas Quarry I: Grotte à Hominidés fossils, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Published 773 ± 4 ka context-age interval; endpoints retain the reported uncertainty, not a period of continuous occupation.
evidence.summary: Hominin remains occur around the Matuyama–Brunhes magnetic reversal.
evidence.limits: Morphological affinities inform competing evolutionary interpretations; they do not prove direct ancestry of Homo sapiens. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Contrebandiers Cave: worked bone and occupation, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Bone tools and animal-processing evidence suggest work on hides and fur in this coastal cave.
evidence.limits: Hide-working is an interpretation of tool form and use; no preserved garment is demonstrated. The deposits contain multiple episodes. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Bizmoune Cave: early shell ornaments, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Minimum-age interpretation from U-series and stratigraphy. The source reports ≥142 ka with substantial dating uncertainty; a single threshold anchor avoids inventing an older bound.
evidence.summary: Perforated marine shells from layer 4c provide early evidence interpreted as personal ornament use.
evidence.limits: A dated overlying speleothem constrains the context. The threshold is not the ornaments’ exact age, and their social meaning or ethnic affiliation is unknown. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Ifri n’Ammar: lower occupation I, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: The lower occupation preserves an early Middle Palaeolithic lithic assemblage.
evidence.limits: Thermoluminescence dates heated material; the uncertainty interval is not the duration of a settlement. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Ifri n’Ammar: early tanged-tool phase, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A younger occupation in the same sequence contains tanged pieces.
evidence.limits: An Aterian technological label describes artefacts; it does not identify an ethnic people or prove migration. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Ifri n’Ammar: upper occupation sequence, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Later Middle Palaeolithic occupation is documented in Upper OS.
evidence.limits: This is a distinct excavated phase, separated from the older dated occupations; occupation continuity is not assumed. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Rhafas Cave: early Middle Stone Age, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A stratified lithic assemblage anchors an early phase of activity in the cave.
evidence.limits: Luminescence dates sediment deposition; unit association and uncertainty matter when assigning artefact ages. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Rhafas Cave: later Middle Stone Age terrace, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A younger terrace assemblage records later Middle Stone Age activity.
evidence.limits: This phase is not evidence for an unchanged population throughout the much longer cave sequence. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Rhafas Cave: Later Stone Age terrace, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: The terrace preserves a Later Stone Age occupation before the requested cutoff.
evidence.limits: Younger terrace material around 15.4 ka falls outside this pre-15,000 BCE inventory. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Dar es-Soltan 1: bone-tool occupation near Rabat
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A shaped rib implement was recovered from an Aterian archaeological context.
evidence.limits: A possible knife function is supported by manufacture and wear analysis; its exact task is not certain. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: El Mnasra: earliest modeled cave occupation, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Combined OSL/US-ESR Bayesian model in Ben Arous et al. (2022), Table 4, for US 9d. Numeric placement uses 1950 minus modeled age.
evidence.summary: Anthropogenic sediments in US 9d mark the earliest reported human presence in the cave sequence.
evidence.limits: A modeled stratigraphic-unit interval, not continuous residence or a direct date on a diagnostic human fossil. Later occupations and technological changes are separate from this marker. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or population estimate.

evidence.title: El Harhoura 2: earlier cave occupations, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: The cave preserves Middle Palaeolithic activity in the Rabat–Témara coastal area.
evidence.limits: A site-specific sediment chronology supports the phase; tool tradition alone does not identify biological lineage. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: El Harhoura 2: late Middle Palaeolithic occupation
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A substantially younger occupation is recorded in the same cave.
evidence.limits: This phase does not fill the intervening gaps in occupation. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Taforalt: Middle Stone Age shell ornaments, Morocco
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Perforated marine shells and use traces support personal ornament use inland from the coast.
evidence.limits: Shell movement indicates transport; it does not fix a migration route or the identity of the wearers. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Taforalt: terminal Middle Stone Age occupation
evidence.dateLabel: ~24.5 ka calibrated BP; late MSA anchor
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian modelling of AMS radiocarbon dates reported as calibrated BP. Numeric conversion uses the 1950 BP epoch.
evidence.summary: A non-Levallois flake assemblage persisted before the later bladelet-based occupation.
evidence.limits: This is the dated late end of the observed MSA sequence, not the origin or extinction of a population. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Taforalt: established Iberomaurusian occupation
evidence.dateLabel: Present by at least 21,160 calibrated BP
evidence.dateBasis: Published minimum antiquity of the LSA occurrence from AMS/Bayesian chronology. It is a threshold anchor, not an invented duration.
evidence.summary: The dated cave sequence places Iberomaurusian bladelet technology here before 15,000 BCE.
evidence.limits: This minimum-age anchor does not claim the tradition began exactly then. The well-known ~15 ka burials are later than this inventory’s cutoff. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Haua Fteah: possible earliest cave visits, Libya
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Sparse lithic evidence may indicate visits near the base of the excavated cave sequence.
evidence.limits: The authors qualify the earliest visits as possible; most early occupation evidence is later and intermittent. No species assignment follows from the tools. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Haua Fteah: human mandibles, Libya
evidence.dateBasis: Modelled context age reported by Jacobs et al.; interval expresses chronological uncertainty and stratigraphic placement.
evidence.summary: Two mandibles attributed to Homo sapiens occur in the Levalloiso-Mousterian sequence.
evidence.limits: Context dating is not a direct date on each fossil. Archaeological labels do not imply a Levantine origin or an exact travel route. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Haua Fteah: Dabban layer XX occupation
evidence.dateBasis: Published modelled age interval for layer XX, after the Douka et al. chronology summarized in Table 1.
evidence.summary: Layer XX preserves a younger phase of cave activity within the Dabban sequence.
evidence.limits: Layer chronology does not define a people or prove uninterrupted occupation through the entire Dabban span. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Haua Fteah: Dabban layer XVII occupation
evidence.dateBasis: Published age interval for layer XVII in Table 1; this layer estimate is based on a single radiocarbon sample and correlated stratigraphy, not a dense series of direct dates.
evidence.summary: This later dated layer documents cave use during the last glacial period.
evidence.limits: It is a separate stratigraphic observation, not a second name for layer XX. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Oued el Akarit: Sondage 8 occupation, Tunisia
evidence.dateLabel: 44.10–42.65 ka cal BP; OSL estimates are younger
evidence.dateBasis: Map uses the published 95.4% calibrated AMS range, 44,100–42,650 cal BP. Original AMS age is 39,550 ± 400 radiocarbon BP; adjacent OSL ages ~37.3 ± 2.0–2.5 ka are retained as a discrepancy, not averaged or mistaken for calibrated radiocarbon.
evidence.summary: Burnt material, refitting flakes and a trampled surface identify a Middle Stone Age occupation beside freshwater resources.
evidence.limits: The direct eggshell radiocarbon result differs from contextual OSL estimates around 37.3 ka. The chronology is not treated as unanimously resolved. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Bété I: rainforest-associated occupations, Côte d’Ivoire
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Dated tool assemblages occur with environmental evidence for wet tropical forest.
evidence.limits: The broad unit contains separate horizons; it does not demonstrate uninterrupted settlement, population size or direct ancestry of current forest peoples. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Bété I: younger Middle Stone Age occupation, Côte d’Ivoire
evidence.dateLabel: ~20 ka to 15,000 BCE cutoff; eligible part of Unit C
evidence.dateBasis: OSL unit estimate ~20–12 ka, explicitly clipped at astronomical year -14999 (15,000 BCE; 16,949 years before 1950). Unit-wide bounds do not locate individual tools exactly within that interval.
evidence.summary: A younger assemblage shows Middle Stone Age technology persisting in the Anyama area.
evidence.limits: Unit C is dated ~20–12 ka. Only its older portion is displayed; the cutoff is an editorial boundary, not abandonment or a dated cultural transition. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Bargny 1: Middle Pleistocene occupation, Senegal
evidence.dateBasis: Ben Arous et al. (2024) updates the earlier 150 ± 6 ka OSL estimate. Display covers both quoted updated uncertainty ranges (152–124 ka); this envelope is not a combined confidence interval. Numeric placement uses 1950 minus age.
evidence.summary: Stone artefacts document early Middle Stone Age activity near the Atlantic coastal zone.
evidence.limits: An occupation near a coast does not establish a coastal migration route or maritime specialization. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Tiémassas: earlier Middle Stone Age occupation, Senegal
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: The earlier dated assemblage records toolmaking near the Nianing coastal area.
evidence.limits: The rounded age is not an exact year. Site coordinates are generalized from the published locality description and map. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Tiémassas: middle occupation phase, Senegal
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: An intermediate dated assemblage uses Levallois and discoidal reduction.
evidence.limits: Technological similarities between visits do not demonstrate biological or ethnic continuity. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Tiémassas: later Middle Stone Age occupation, Senegal
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: The younger excavated assemblage documents continued use of Middle Stone Age techniques.
evidence.limits: The record comprises separate dated episodes, not a continuously inhabited settlement lasting 37,000 years. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Ravin Blanc I: early Middle Stone Age, Senegal
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A stratified assemblage near the Falémé contains heavy-duty and smaller stone tools.
evidence.limits: The plotted interval is the combined outer envelope of the two reported uncertainties, not a formal combined confidence interval or an occupation duration. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Ounjougou: early Levallois evidence, Mali
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: An early Levallois core provides evidence of human activity within the Ounjougou complex.
evidence.limits: This is sparse evidence within a broad chronological bracket; later dated assemblages must not be projected backward as an unchanged population. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Ounjougou: later stratified occupation sequence, Mali
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Numerous stratified tool assemblages show changing technical practices in the Yamé valley.
evidence.limits: This single complex-level marker summarizes more than 30 levels; it is not 30 new mapped sites, continuous residence or evidence of a named ethnic group. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Laminia: Middle Stone Age river-bar activity, Senegal
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Tools occur on a stabilized gravel-bar surface of the Gambia River in southeastern Senegal.
evidence.limits: The river name does not place this site in the modern country of The Gambia. The later Saxomununya assemblage in the same paper lies outside the cutoff. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Birimi: Middle Stone Age assemblages, Ghana
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Buried stone artefacts document Pleistocene activity on the Gambaga Escarpment.
evidence.limits: The broad published chronology is retained instead of presenting ~40 ka as exact. Later Kintampo and other deposits at this multi-period site are excluded. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Sodmein Cave: Middle Palaeolithic occupation, Egypt
evidence.dateLabel: 118 ± 8 ka; mean TL age of Level 5
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Burnt flints and large combustion features document cave use in the Eastern Desert.
evidence.limits: The reported mean summarizes multiple measurements; it does not establish a 16,000-year permanent settlement. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Taramsa 1: child burial in a quarry landscape, Egypt
evidence.dateBasis: TAR-3 fill sample age reported in the 2010 primary chapter. The quoted uncertainty is retained; earlier and conflicting dates discussed by the excavators are not silently harmonized.
evidence.summary: A child skeleton attributed to Homo sapiens was found in a pit within a landscape of chert extraction.
evidence.limits: The date comes from burial-fill context, not direct dating of the skeleton. Published conflicting determinations and associations require caution; this is not a residential village. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Nazlet Khater 2: Pleistocene human burial, Egypt
evidence.dateBasis: Published ESR estimate summarized by Wurz and Van Peer; interval is the reported dating uncertainty, not duration of occupation.
evidence.summary: A Homo sapiens skeleton was recovered in the Nazlet Khater quarrying landscape.
evidence.limits: Association with nearby mining activity and context chronology should not be mistaken for an exact date or an ethnic affiliation. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Bîr Tarfawi: Grey 1 archaeological lake context, Egypt
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Middle Stone Age evidence is associated with former water-supported landscapes in today’s desert.
evidence.limits: The measurement dates a sedimentary lake phase at BT-14, not a human fossil or a particular hearth. Archaeology and environmental context must remain distinct. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Bîr Sahara East: West 4 archaeological context, Egypt
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: A younger lake phase provides a chronological context for Middle Stone Age activity in the adjacent basin.
evidence.limits: The revised date does not demonstrate that this lake phase and Bîr Tarfawi’s Green phase were simultaneous. Individual visits are not directly dated by the lake sample. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Sai Island 8-B-11: early occupation sequence, Sudan
evidence.dateBasis: Published age estimates; numeric placement uses 1950 minus age in years. Rounded deep-time ages are not exact calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Successive archaeological levels include Acheulean and Sangoan assemblages, grinding evidence and pigment processing.
evidence.limits: These technological labels are analytical categories. Interstratification does not establish a simple species replacement or one continuous resident population. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.

evidence.title: Wadi Kubbaniya: Late Palaeolithic occupation complex, Egypt
evidence.dateBasis: Calibrated phase range in Leplongeon’s Table 1, based on published site chronologies. It is not a direct conversion of uncalibrated dates in older field reports.
evidence.summary: Repeated camps and activity areas occur in the wadi’s Late Palaeolithic landscape.
evidence.limits: This is a complex-level phase marker, not a date for every excavated camp. Kubbaniyan names a lithic classification, not a known ethnic people; no population count is inferred. Point is an approximate locality, not a territorial boundary or a population estimate.
